Sorry, I wasn't clear. This statement:

>The QBs who are tops in both are no doubt the greatest passers ever.

is inaccurate, because ANY/A and passer rating use nearly the same information to come at very similar results. They both use completion percentage, yards per attempt, touchdown percentage, and interception percentage to rank players. Anyone who does well in those four categories will rank highly in both.

The differences between the two systems is primarily that ANY/A also includes sacks. Therefore, if a QB ranks better in passer rating than ANY/A, it's because they took more sacks than their ANY/A peers.

This is easy to prove. Go to the above link and compare the sack percentage rankings for QBs in the top 20 of ANY/A and passer rating. 15 QBs on each list are the same, so we only need to look at the 10 unique QBs:

- ANY/A: Player A, Player B, Player C, Player D, and Player E. **Avg Sack% of 120.6**
- Passer Rating: Player F, Player G, Player H, Player I, Player J. **Avg Sack% of 97.4**

See the difference? The index stats scale so 100 is league average, meaning the 5 passer rating QBs had a combined *below league average sack rate*! Meanwhile the ANY/A QBs were more than a standard deviation above average!

When considering the greatest passers ever, there's no need to look at passer rating. It provides *less* information than ANY/A and is therefore a less accurate metric for judging QBs.
